title: Rising Temperatures Threaten Europe’s Food Supply and Prices
subtitle: Extreme heat and drought across the continent are causing crop losses, leading to concerns about higher costs for consumers.

summary.en: Farmers across Europe are facing a difficult season as extreme heat and drought damage essential food crops. Major products like olive oil, wine, and vegetables are seeing lower production levels. The European Union has already lowered its harvest expectations for several important items. Experts warn that these supply issues will likely lead to higher prices for shoppers in the coming months. While some regions remain resilient, the overall impact on the agricultural economy is significant.
summary.zh: 歐洲各地的農民正經歷艱難的季節，極端高溫與乾旱損害了重要的糧食作物。橄欖油、葡萄酒與蔬菜等主要產品的產量均呈現下滑。歐盟已下調多項重要農產品的收成預期。專家警告，這些供應問題很可能導致未來幾個月消費者的購物成本增加。儘管部分地區仍展現韌性，但對農業經濟的整體影響依然顯著。

paragraphs.en: Farmers across Europe are warning of a serious drop in food production as extreme heat, drought, and wildfires damage crops. From maize to fresh salads, the continent’s agricultural sector is struggling to keep up with the changing climate. As temperatures reach new record highs, the cost of many basic food items is expected to rise, creating new economic challenges for both producers and consumers.
paragraphs.zh: 歐洲各地的農民正發出警告，指出極端高溫、乾旱與野火正損害農作物，導致糧食產量嚴重下滑。從玉米到新鮮沙拉蔬菜，歐洲的農業部門正竭力應對氣候變遷帶來的衝擊。隨著氣溫屢創新高，許多基本食品的成本預計將會上漲，這對生產者與消費者而言，都帶來了新的經濟挑戰。

paragraphs.en: The vegetable growers association, Légumes de France, reported that thousands of tonnes of produce have been lost. This includes common items like carrots, onions, garlic, and salad leaves. In some cases, production is expected to be cut in half because of the lack of rain. These losses represent tens of millions of euros in value, highlighting the scale of the problem for the European food market.
paragraphs.zh: 蔬菜種植者協會「法國蔬菜 (Légumes de France)」指出，已有數千噸的農產品損失。這包括胡蘿蔔、洋蔥、大蒜與沙拉葉等常見品項。在某些情況下，由於缺乏雨水，產量預計將減半。這些損失價值高達數千萬歐元，凸顯了歐洲食品市場面臨的問題規模之大。

paragraphs.en: Wine production is also facing a difficult year. In famous French regions such as Champagne, Bordeaux, and Burgundy, the scorching weather has slowed the growth of grapes. According to The Guardian, producers in Champagne expect the earliest harvest in history, with picking likely to begin in mid-August. This is about a month earlier than what was normal just a few decades ago. Furthermore, grape yields are expected to be about 10% smaller than last year.
paragraphs.zh: 葡萄酒生產也面臨艱難的一年。在香檳 (Champagne)、波爾多 (Bordeaux) 與勃根地 (Burgundy) 等法國知名產區，酷熱天氣減緩了葡萄的生長。根據《衛報 (The Guardian)》報導，香檳產區的生產者預計將迎來史上最早的採收期，採摘工作可能在八月中旬展開。這比幾十年前的正常時間提早了約一個月。此外，葡萄產量預計將比去年減少約百分之十。

paragraphs.en: Cereal crops are also suffering. In Spain, the ministry of agriculture predicts that the 2026-27 cereal harvest will fall significantly, dropping from 24 million tonnes last year to just over 18.5 million tonnes. This forecast was made even before the recent wildfires caused additional damage to the land. The European Union has also lowered its harvest predictions for many other products. Expectations for sunflowers, which are essential for cooking oils, have fallen by 7%. Grain maize is down 6%, while potatoes and soya beans have seen their production forecasts trimmed by 3%.
paragraphs.zh: 穀物作物也同樣受創。在西班牙，農業部預測二零二六至二七年度的穀物收成將大幅下滑，從去年的兩千四百萬噸降至僅剩一千八百五十萬噸多一點。這項預測甚至是在近期野火對土地造成額外損害之前所做出的。歐盟也下調了許多其他農產品的收成預測。作為烹飪油關鍵原料的葵花籽，產量預期下調了百分之七；穀物玉米減少了百分之六，而馬鈴薯與大豆的產量預測則被調降了百分之三。

paragraphs.en: Olive oil, which has already been expensive for some time, is expected to see another price increase. Producers are struggling with a combination of extreme heat, drought, and fires. In countries like Greece, Italy, and Portugal, olive groves have been burned. Even the trees that were not touched by fire have suffered from poor air quality and ash. Sarah Vachon, the founder of the Citizens of Soil olive oil group, noted that unless the weather improves soon, prices will likely rise in the autumn because there will be less fruit available to make oil.
paragraphs.zh: 橄欖油的價格本已居高不下，預計將再次上漲。生產者正苦於應對極端高溫、乾旱與火災的夾擊。在希臘、義大利與葡萄牙等國，橄欖園慘遭祝融。即便未受火災波及的樹木，也因空氣品質不佳與落塵而受損。橄欖油組織「土壤公民 (Citizens of Soil)」創辦人莎拉·瓦雄 (Sarah Vachon) 指出，除非天氣能儘快好轉，否則秋季價格很可能會上漲，因為能用來製油的果實將會減少。

paragraphs.en: Despite these challenges, the impact is not the same everywhere. Some countries have been more fortunate. For example, Romania has seen more rainfall, and Italy’s wheat crop has shown that it can be resilient, or able to recover well from difficult conditions. However, the ASAJA agricultural trade body explained that the damage is widespread. They noted that fires have hit orchards, vineyards, and greenhouses, affecting everything from almonds and avocados to citrus fruits. A spokesperson for the group said that while lower production might mean fewer exports, the main concern for the industry is the rising cost of production rather than limits on international trade.
paragraphs.zh: 儘管面臨這些挑戰，各地的影響程度並不相同。有些國家較為幸運。例如，羅馬尼亞的降雨量較多，而義大利的小麥作物也展現出韌性，即在艱困條件下仍能良好恢復的能力。然而，農業貿易團體「西班牙青年農民農業協會 (ASAJA)」解釋說，損害範圍相當廣泛。他們指出，火災已波及果園、葡萄園與溫室，影響範圍涵蓋從杏仁、酪梨到柑橘類水果等各類作物。該組織發言人表示，雖然產量下降可能意味著出口減少，但產業目前最擔憂的並非國際貿易限制，而是生產成本的攀升。

paragraphs.en: This situation is especially difficult because the price of olive oil had already been high for two years. This previous spike was caused by a mix of high demand, dry weather, and the spread of pests and diseases. While prices had started to drift down slightly, they remain high in many stores. In the UK, for example, the average price for a one-litre bottle of extra virgin olive oil remains above £7 and has begun to climb again in recent months.
paragraphs.zh: 這種情況之所以特別棘手，是因為橄欖油價格在過去兩年本就處於高檔。先前的價格飆漲是由高需求、乾燥氣候以及病蟲害蔓延等多重因素所致。雖然價格近期已開始略微回落，但在許多商店中依然維持高價。以英國為例，一公升裝特級初榨橄欖油的平均價格仍維持在七英鎊以上，且近幾個月已開始再次攀升。

paragraphs.en: Looking ahead, the agricultural sector faces a long-term challenge. Even in places like Spain, where farmers are well-adapted to hot and dry conditions, the current weather is testing the limits of their systems. Farmers there have been using more irrigation—a system of moving water to land to help crops grow—and better water storage to manage the drought. However, as the climate continues to change, the industry must find new ways to protect its harvests. For now, consumers should prepare for the possibility of higher grocery bills as the effects of this summer's heat continue to ripple through the global economy.
paragraphs.zh: 展望未來，農業部門面臨著長期挑戰。即便是在農民早已適應炎熱乾燥氣候的西班牙等地，當前的天氣狀況也正在考驗其系統的極限。當地的農民一直在增加灌溉——即將水引至土地以協助作物生長的系統——並利用更好的儲水設施來應對乾旱。然而，隨著氣候持續變遷，產業必須尋找保護收成的新方法。目前，消費者應做好心理準備，隨著今年夏季高溫的影響持續波及全球經濟，食品雜貨帳單可能會變得更加昂貴。

keyTerms.definitionEn: To manage to stay at the same level or pace as something that is changing or moving.
keyTerms.noteZh: 這裡指農業部門難以應對氣候變遷的速度。文中：the continent’s agricultural sector is struggling to keep up with the changing climate.

keyTerms.definitionEn: To reduce the amount or size of something slightly.
keyTerms.noteZh: 常見作名詞（裝飾）或修剪頭髮，這裡指預測數據的下調。文中：Grain maize is down 6%, while potatoes and soya beans have seen their production forecasts trimmed by 3%.
這裡形容價格緩慢地下降，而非指物體漂流。文中：While prices had started to drift down slightly, they remain high in many stores.

keyTerms.definitionEn: To spread through a system or group of people like waves.
keyTerms.noteZh: 常見作名詞（漣漪），這裡指影響力在經濟體系中擴散。文中：consumers should prepare for the possibility of higher grocery bills as the effects of this summer's heat continue to ripple through the global economy.

quiz.question: What change has occurred regarding the grape harvest in the Champagne region compared to previous decades?

options.A: The harvest will be delayed by one month due to the scorching weather.
options.B: The harvest will begin about a month earlier than it typically did in the past.
options.C: The harvest will be 10% larger than last year due to the early start.
options.D: The harvest has been completely cancelled due to widespread wildfires.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 B。根據文章第三段，Champagne 地區的葡萄採收期預計將在八月中旬開始，這比過去幾十年來的正常時間早了一個月。選項 A 錯誤，因為文章說是「提早」而非「延後」。選項 C 錯誤，因為文章提到產量反而會減少 10%。選項 D 錯誤，文章並未提到採收被取消，僅提到產量下降。

quiz.question: Based on the article, why might consumers see higher prices for olive oil in the coming months?

options.A: Because international trade agreements have restricted the export of olive oil.
options.B: Because the demand for olive oil has completely disappeared in European markets.
options.C: Because the combination of fire damage and poor weather has reduced the available supply of olives.
options.D: Because farmers have successfully increased their production costs through better irrigation.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 C。根據第五段，橄欖油生產商面臨極端高溫、乾旱與野火的雙重打擊，導致橄欖樹受損，Sarah Vachon 指出因果關係：由於可用的橄欖果實減少，價格將在秋季上漲。選項 A 錯誤，文中提到產業主要擔心的是生產成本，而非貿易限制。選項 B 錯誤，文中並未提到需求消失。選項 D 錯誤，生產成本上升是負面影響，並非農民主動追求的結果。

quiz.question: In the sixth paragraph, what does the word 'resilient' mean in the context of Italy’s wheat crop?

options.A: Able to withstand or recover quickly from difficult conditions.
options.B: Highly sensitive to changes in temperature and water levels.
options.C: Completely destroyed by the recent fires and extreme heat.
options.D: Producing a record-breaking amount of grain despite the drought.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 A。文中提到「Italy’s wheat crop has shown that it can be resilient, or able to recover well from difficult conditions」，作者直接在逗號後提供了定義。選項 B 與 resillient 的意義相反。選項 C 錯誤，文中提到該作物展現了韌性，並非被摧毀。選項 D 雖然提到恢復，但文中並未說明產量是否打破紀錄，僅強調其適應與恢復能力。

quiz.question: What is the primary message of the article regarding the European agricultural sector?

options.A: European farmers are successfully using new technology to completely eliminate the effects of climate change.
options.B: The primary issue facing European agriculture is a lack of interest from the younger generation.
options.C: Extreme weather conditions are causing significant agricultural losses, leading to higher food costs and long-term economic challenges.
options.D: The European Union has decided to stop all food exports to focus on domestic consumption.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 C。全文從第一段開始即點出氣候變遷（高溫、乾旱、野火）對歐洲農業造成的損害，並在後續段落詳細說明各類農產品（蔬菜、葡萄酒、穀物、橄欖油）的減產，最後總結這將導致消費者面臨更高的物價與長期的經濟挑戰。選項 A 過於樂觀，與文意不符；選項 B 文中未提及；選項 D 則是錯誤的推論，文章並未提到停止出口的政策。
